To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

merlin, a tumor suppressor protein, interacts with a cell adhesion molecule, beta1 integrins, and that merlin's subcellular localization changes from cytoplasmic in undifferentiated Schwann cells to subplasmalemmal in myelinating Schwann cells.

merlin is a 68-kDa cytosolic protein in neurons and a 68-, 88-, and 120-kDa protein in Schwann cells, that merlin translocates to the cytoskeletal compartment in Schwann cells undergoing differentiation into myelinated axons, that beta1 integrin coimmunoprecepitates with the 68- and 88-kDa merlin proteins, and that merlin is localized to the cytoskeleton in Schwann cells in

merlin is present in the cytoplasm of Schwann cells (a cell type involved in the formation of schwannomas), that it is present in the plasma membrane and cytoplasm of differentiated myelinating Schwann cells, and that it associates with beta1 integrins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of merlin tumor suppressor function in the peripheral nervous system.
the role of merlin in SC differentiation and myelination, and the molecular mechanisms of how merlin functions as an inhibitor of cell proliferation.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate SC differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
merlin, the neurofi bromatosis 2 gene product and beta1 integrins associate in isolated and differentiated SCs.
the 88- and the 120-kDa proteins are merlin-related proteins and that merlin interacts in a beta1 integrin-dependent manner with cytoskeletal components.
merlin is a cytoplasmic protein in undifferentiated cells, but translocates to the cytoskeleton in differentiating myelinating cells, and associates with beta1 integrins in both cell states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

merlin and beta1 integrins are expressed in isolated and differentially SC/N cultures, that merlin is predominantly soluble in undifferentiated cultures but insoluble in differentiating cultures, and that merlin and integrin are associated in both undifferentiated and differentiating SC/N cells.
merlin is expressed in both neurons and Schwann cells and that it is associated with the beta1 integrin in Schwann cells.
merlin is a cytosolic protein in undifferentiated Schwann cells and becomes associated with beta1 integrins in the plasma membrane of differentiating cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

merlin, a tumor suppressor gene product that is mutated in neurofibromatous type 2, associates with the beta1 integrin subunit of the extracellular matrix receptor, integrin, during the differentiation of Schwann cells into myelinating glia.
Merlin, the neurofibro-matosis type 1 (NF1) gene product, and the beta 1 integrin associate with each other in isolated and different-iating Schwann cells (Schwann cell, SC).
merlin is a dynamic protein that changes location and associates with beta1 integrins as SCs differentiate.
